title: Leakage Resilience Under an Invertible Random Permutation
summary: The leakage-resilience proof covers a random transformation, while its extension to an invertible random permutation remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: Extend the leakage-resilience proof from a random transformation to an invertible random permutation.

scope.domain: Leakage-resilience security analysis for sponge-based authenticated encryption.
parameters: Random transformation, the model covered by the existing proof
Invertible random permutation, the target model for the extension
Slae or the underlying FGHF' construction, the construction being analyzed
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the leakage-resilience analysis of Slae or the underlying FGHF' construction to an invertible random permutation and derive corresponding security bounds.

citations.label: Sponges Resist Leakage: The Case of Authenticated Encryption

progress.summary: The source presents the random-transformation case as analyzed, while describing the invertible-random-permutation case as an additional layer of complexity that was not pursued.
citation_labels: Jean Paul Degabriele et al., Sponges Resist Leakage: The Case of Authenticated Encryption
